issue.title: mflo/mfhi hazard nop placed after label when the intervening instruction is j
issue.body:
When a single instruction separates mflo/mfhi from a mult/div, and that instruction is a branch, maspsx correctly puts the hazard nop in the branch delay slot, before any following label. For j, it puts the nop after the label instead:

Expected (ASPSX):  `mflo; j $L_end; nop; $L_div: divu`
Actual (maspsx):  `mflo; j $L_end; $L_div: nop; divu`

The instructions are identical, but $L_div marks the nop. In a switch, the jump-table entry for a case starting with divu then points one instruction early. Found in Final Fantasy VII, in a switch where a case ending in mflo; j is immediately followed in memory by a case starting with divu.

Scratches (same C, gcc 2.7.2, ASPSX 2.56):
 - (correct) [aspsx](https://decomp.me/scratch/l0N43) (PsyQ 4.0, real ASPSX)
 - (incorrect) [maspsx](https://decomp.me/scratch/Hi7fQ) --aspsx-version=2.56

FF7 uses 2.34. maspsx produces the same incorrect output there, and real ASPSX 2.34 places the nop before the label. I checked this with a minimal case under dosemu2, which I can add as an aspsx/ fixture.

I have a fix and tests ready to open as a PR.

expected.cause: _handle_mflo_mfhi in maspsx/__init__.py only emits the hazard nop before the following label (in the delay slot) when the single intervening instruction is in branch_mnemonics; jump mnemonics such as j were not included, so for j the nop lands after the label.
